title: Cutting program operating costs by 40% ($72K) while keeping outcomes
situation: I managed CityU's yearly 17-week Amazon AWS Military Apprenticeship Program, which trained military veterans and spouses in Linux administration, networking, databases, programming and full-stack development. The program's instructor and teaching assistant staffing model was expensive and unevenly loaded.
task: Reduce operating costs without hurting apprentices' learning or their placement into Amazon on-the-job training (OJT).
action: I analyzed how instructor and TA hours were spent across modules and found overlaps and underused time [confirm: specific inefficiencies, e.g., redundant sessions or misaligned TA coverage]. I restructured assignments so instructors focused on high-value teaching while TAs handled labs and support, reused course materials across cohorts, and ran the program on Kanban and Scrum so workload stayed visible. I made the changes together with the 5 instructors and 5 TAs I led, not just announced them, so quality didn't drop.
result: The program saved $72,000 over 2 years, cutting the operating budget by 40%, and 93% of participants still moved on to OJT with Amazon's AWS team. What I learned: cost and quality aren't automatically a tradeoff. Fixing how work is structured can improve both.
